page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per socket. The system comes provisioned with 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 3,800 GB NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in multi-core and memory-heavy workloads. The server achieves top-tier performance in PassMark memory testing, large-block memory read bandwidth (464.12 GB/sec), and large-block memory write bandwidth (215.66 GB/sec). Database and caching operations display notable capacity, logging 134.09 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier PassMark database operation scores. Multi-threaded compilation and multi-core Geekbench scores also place in the upper tier, driven by the 64 dedicated physical cores. In contrast, single-core execution metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, operate within the middle 50% tier.

The qualitative cost profile favors workloads requiring massive memory capacity and low-latency storage per compute unit. Using dedicated Neoverse-V2 physical cores eliminates virtualization contention and hyperthreading resource competition, offering higher sustained throughput per core relative to typical SMT-based instances. However, the arm64 architecture lacks x86-specific vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX, and the absence of discrete GPUs limits raw acceleration for large-model training.

The r8gd.16xlarge is engineered for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, large-scale relational databases, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency software build pipelines that leverage high memory bandwidth and local NVMe caching.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated cores on the arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 512 GB of RAM (8 GB per core), 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a 30 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance exhibits top-tier multi-threaded compute, high memory bandwidth, and standout database processing, reaching 134.09 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. While single-thread execution rates and vector-heavy compute remain mid-tier due to the absence of x86 vector extensions and dedicated GPUs, the dedicated core layout eliminates SMT contention. This configuration is tailored for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory key-value stores, distributed transactional databases, big data analytics, and continuous software compilation pipelines.
